name: Missing override annotation
description: Flags a function or event that overrides an inherited member without a `; @override` annotation on the header or the line above it. Disabled by default. The fix adds `; @override` to the header.
definition: Flags, as an `[info]`, a top-level `Function` or `Event` declared on this script that shares its name with a member on the script it `Extends` (directly or transitively) and is not marked with a `; @override` annotation on the header line or the line immediately above it. Papyrus has no language-level `override` keyword, so the annotation is a convention (same family as `@nodiscard` / `@deprecated` / `@private`) that makes an intentional override visible next to the declaration. Distinct from `function-override`, which only informs that a name collision with an ancestor exists; this rule requires the marker. Only checked when an `Extends` chain can be resolved from project context. A function declared inside a `State` block is not checked (state-based override is a separate mechanism from `Extends`). Disabled by default, since most existing scripts have no override convention yet; opt in with `rules.missing_override`. Automatically fixable: the fix appends `; @override` to the declaration header (or `@override` onto an existing trailing comment), matching the lookback this rule itself reads.
